#### 2. Check and Deal with Data Problems
#### Check for duplicated rows
```{r}
duplicated_rows <- data[duplicated(data), ]
if (nrow(duplicated_rows) > 0) {
  print("Duplicated rows found!")
} else {
  print("No duplicated rows found!")
  data <- unique(data) # Remove duplicates
}
missing_values <- sum(is.na(data))
if (missing_values > 0) {
  print("Missing values found!")
  # You can choose to remove missing values or impute them here
  # Example: Remove rows with missing values
  data <- na.omit(data)
} else {
  print("No missing values found!")
}



missing_values <- sum(is.na(data))

if (missing_values > 0) {
  print("Missing values found!")
  
  # Impute missing values
  # Here, you can choose a method for imputation such as mean, median, or mode
  
  #  Impute missing values with the mean of each column
  for (col in names(data)) {
    if (is.numeric(data[[col]])) {
      data[[col]][is.na(data[[col]])] <- mean(data[[col]], na.rm = TRUE)
    }
  }
} else {
  print("No missing values found!")
}
```

#### 3. Variables important for PCA
#### Selecting numerical columns
```{r}
check_variance <- function(data) {
  variable_names <- names(data)  # Get the names of all variables in the dataset
  for (variable in variable_names) {
    # Calculate variance for each variable
    variance <- var(data[[variable]])  # Compute the variance using var() function
    cat("Variance of", variable, ":", variance, "\n")  # Print the variable name and its variance
  }
}

numeric_data <- data[, sapply(data, is.numeric)]  # Select only numeric variables
variances <- apply(numeric_data, 2, var)  # Compute variances for each numeric variable
print(variances)


```
#### 4. Variables important for PCA
#### Selecting numerical columns
```{r}
pca_result <- prcomp(numeric_data, scale. = TRUE)  # scale. = TRUE scales the variables to have unit variance

# Summary of PCA
summary(pca_result)

# Plotting PCA
biplot(pca_result, scale = 0)


```
#### 5. Apply a PCA to study variables correlation and project individuals into 2D plan.
```{r}


plot(pca_result)

pc1_loadings <- pca_result$rotation[, 1]  
pc2_loadings <- pca_result$rotation[, 2]  

prop_var <- pca_result$sdev^2 / sum(pca_result$sdev^2) 
plot(prop_var)
```
#### 6. Are the part-time job, weekly self study and extracurricular activities effect on student performances ?
```{r}

# Example of a total score (sum of several exam scores)
data$total_score <- rowSums(data[, c("math_score", "history_score", 
                                     "physics_score", "chemistry_score", 
                                     "biology_score", "english_score", 
                                     "geography_score")], na.rm = TRUE)

# Scatter plot to examine relationships
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(data, aes(x = weekly_self_study_hours, y = total_score)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", col = "blue") +
  labs(title = "Weekly Self-Study Hours vs. Total Score")

# Boxplot to compare part-time job effect on performance
ggplot(data, aes(x = as.factor(part_time_job), y = total_score)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(x = "Part-Time Job", y = "Total Score", title = "Part-Time Job Effect on Performance")

# Boxplot to compare extracurricular activities' effect on performance
ggplot(data, aes(x = as.factor(extracurricular_activities), y = total_score)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(x = "Extracurricular Activities", y = "Total Score", title = "Extracurricular Activities Effect on Performance")

```
#### 7. Apply a k-means clustering of individuals over the obtained plain.

```{r}
# Perform k-means clustering
k <- 3  # Example: Choosing the number of clusters
kmeans_result <- kmeans(pca_result$x[,1:2], centers = k)

# Plot k-means clusters
plot(pca_result$x[,1:2], col = kmeans_result$cluster, main = "k-means Clustering of Individuals")
points(kmeans_result$centers, col = 1:k, pch = 8, cex = 2)


```
#### 8. Give the optimal K (number of clusters).
```{r}


pca_data <- data.frame(pca_result$x[, 1:2], cluster = as.factor(kmeans_result$cluster))


ggplot(pca_data, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = cluster)) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(title = "K-Means Clustering on PCA Plane",
       x = "Principal Component 1",
       y = "Principal Component 2") +
  theme_minimal()


```
